title: Ottawa Ankle & Foot Rules
sources: Stiell IG et al. Ann Emerg Med 1992; JAMA 1993 (validation) — sensitivity ~ 98–100% for clinically significant fractures
purpose: Rules out the need for ankle and foot X-rays after acute blunt injury. Apply to patients ≥ 18 y (validated to age 2 for the ankle rule); unreliable with intoxication, distracting injury, diminished sensation, or > 10 days since injury.

items.label: Bony tenderness at the posterior edge / tip of the LATERAL malleolus (distal 6 cm)
Bony tenderness at the posterior edge / tip of the MEDIAL malleolus (distal 6 cm)
Bony tenderness at the base of the 5th metatarsal
Unable to bear weight (4 steps) both immediately AND in the ED

interpretation.label: No X-ray needed — no malleolar or midfoot pain, no bony tenderness at the named points, and able to bear weight

Imaging indicated — ANKLE series if malleolar-zone pain + tenderness at either malleolus or unable to bear weight; FOOT series if midfoot-zone pain + navicular or base-of-5th-MT tenderness or unable to bear weight
interpretation.disposition: Ankle and/or foot X-ray per the zone

notes: 'Malleolar zone' and 'midfoot zone' are the anatomical triggers; a positive point in a zone only mandates the corresponding series. Bear-weight = transfer weight twice onto each leg, regardless of limping.
buildNote: Rule, not a graded score — any positive point → the relevant film.
